items.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: it is to hear a Gershwin or a Berlin or an Ellington or a Basie tune

ctx.x: Have you been a fan of this music since you were growing up?

Yes. I was a product of the era when everybody else went to Elvis and the Beatles. And I stayed with the big bands, and I stayed with Ellington and Basie and I never moved off of mainstream jazz. Rhythm and melody. I really like the standards. Even the new jazz is really not so much my preference as it is to hear a Gershwin or a Berlin or an Ellington or a Basie tune and hear it done the original way as well as hearing it done today. And I do a lot of that. I call it mixing and matching. Doing the same song done…

I’ve often wondered if we are writing, since the ‘40s especially, is anybody writing standards since then you know? In fact Herbie Hancock just came out with a record and I forget the exact title of it, but what he did was he found what he thought were going to be the standards to come. And he did some more modern tunes but treated them as jazz tunes I guess.
